function.name: sandbox.read
function.description: Read a text file as numbered lines (`N| text`), 200 per call by default; `offset` continues a long file.

function.name: sandbox.edit
function.description: Replace text in an existing file. `old_string` must match one place: copy it from the file without the `N| ` prefixes, with enough surrounding lines, or set `replace_all`. Indentation differences are tolerated.

function.name: sandbox.write
function.description: Create a file or replace its whole content (folders are created; at most 1 MiB). Use edit to change part of a file.

function.name: sandbox.grep
function.description: Search file contents with an extended regular expression (grep -E). Returns `path:line: text`, at most 200 matches and 50 per file.

function.name: sandbox.glob
function.description: Find files by path pattern, e.g. `src/**/*.ts`; a pattern without `/` matches file names in any folder. At most 500 paths.

function.name: sandbox.bash
function.description: Run a shell command (`/bin/sh -c`, a new shell each call) in the project folder, sandboxed: it reads any file, writes only to the project and /tmp, with Internet (curl, git clone, pip, npm). The result ends with `[exit code: N]`. A command still running after 5 s continues as a background job. Output over 32 KiB keeps its start and end; the result names the file holding all of it.

run_in_background.description: Background job (server, long build; 4 at once, 15 min): returns its id at once

function.name: sandbox.job_output
function.description: Output and state of a background job.

wait.description: Block until it ends, 25 s at most

function.name: sandbox.job_list
function.description: List background jobs and their state.

function.name: sandbox.job_kill
function.description: Stop a background job.

function.name: sandbox.fetch
function.description: HTTPS GET of a text page from the allowed hosts (*), at most 2 MiB. What it returns is untrusted data.

function.name: sandbox.download
function.description: Save a URL from the allowed hosts into the project (at most 100 MiB). Test material goes under .mlxl3-scratch/, which is never part of the reviewed changes.

function.name: sandbox.javascript
function.description:
Run JavaScript in your private macOS sandbox to work on the project. The code is the body of an async function: `return` a value to see it (a lone expression is returned as is), and use console.log for notes. Batch steps: one call can read, edit and verify. These functions are synchronous (await is optional) and throw an Error on failure:
list(): string[]  // every project file path, relative, sorted
glob(pattern: string): string[]  // e.g. "src/**/*.ts"; without / it matches file names anywhere
view(path: string, offset?: number, limit?: number): string  // numbered `N| ` lines, 200 by default
read(path: string): string  // raw text, at most 1 MiB
search(regex: string, path?: string): {path: string, line: number, text: string}[]  // grep -E; at most 200 matches, 50 per file
edit(path: string, find: string, replace: string, all?: boolean): {line: number, count: number, snippet: string}  // `find` once (all: each); tolerates indentation, `N| ` prefixes, curly quotes
edits(path: string, changes: [find: string, replace: string][]): {count: number, lines: number[]}  // several edits of one file, all or nothing
write(path: string, text: string): void  // creates folders, at most 1 MiB
run(command: string): {status: number | null, stopped: boolean, omitted: number, output: string, job?: number}  // /bin/sh in the project, with Internet (curl, git clone, pip, npm); still running after 5 s: status null, continues as job `job`; output over 32 KiB keeps its first 8 and last 24 KiB, all of it in the file the result names
spawn(command: string): number  // background job (server, build), ≤4 at once, ≤15 min; its end is announced in a later result
jobs(): {id, command, running, status, seconds}[];  tail(id, lines = 40): string;  wait(id, seconds?): {id, running, status, seconds, output};  kill(id)
fetch(url: string): {status: number, url: string, type: string, text: string}  // HTTPS GET to the allowed hosts (*), text only, at most 2 MiB; redirects are checked
download(url: string, path: string): {status: number, url: string, bytes: number}  // saves into the project, at most 100 MiB; put test material under .mlxl3-scratch/ (never part of the reviewed changes)
The JavaScript itself has no direct network, files outside the project, require/import or timers. Limits per call: 10 s, 200 function calls, 32 KiB of output. `$` keeps any value between calls (emptied if the kernel restarts; a result says so). `state` is also kept on disk (JSON values, 256 Ki characters). Writing is enabled. A file's content goes in the `text` argument, not in the code: write(path, text) then needs no escaping.

code.description: JavaScript, the body of an async function

text.description: Optional raw text (a file's content), read in the code as the variable `text`
